text.p: Russia launched a military satellite from the Baikonur cosmodrome in Kazakhstan on Wednesday, a space official said.
A spokesman for the Military Space Forces' headquarters told Reuters the Kosmos-2335 satellite was launched at 3 p.m. (1200 GMT) using a two-stage light Tsiklon-2 booster.
The spokesman said the satellite would be used "in the interests of the defence ministry". He gave no further details.
The first Kosmos satellite was launched in 1962. Most of these probes were used as spy satellites in the Soviet era.

Russian media reported last month that the country had been without photo reconnaisance satellites for nearly two months, after the last operable one burned up on re-entry to the atmosphere on September 28.
At the time a Military Space Forces official denied the reports saying "it is impossible that a superpower such as Russia could be without such satellites".
